name: Chingri Malai Curry
subtitle: prawns in a sweet cardamom-scented coconut milk gravy

ingredients.qty: 500g large, shelled and deveined, heads left on if you have them
1 large, ground to a smooth paste

ingredients.note: the sweetness is characteristic, not a mistake

prepNotes: Rub the prawns with 1/2 tsp turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt and rest 10 minutes, no longer — salt draws water out of prawns fast.
Shake the tin of coconut milk hard, or whisk the thick and thin parts together, before measuring.
Grind the onion without water so the paste fries rather than stews.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil to smoking, cool for 30 seconds, then sear the prawns 45 seconds a side until they just turn pink at the edges. Lift them out immediately.
steps.tip: They are not cooked through at this point and should not be. Prawns need 90 seconds total in the whole recipe.

steps.text: Add the bay leaves, cardamom, cinnamon and cloves to the same oil and let them puff for 20 seconds.
Add the onion paste and fry 7-8 minutes on medium until it turns pale gold and the oil begins to separate.
steps.tip: Do not brown it. This gravy should stay ivory-white, not go tan.

steps.text: Stir in the ginger paste, the remaining turmeric and the kashmiri chilli and cook 1 minute.
Pour in the coconut milk with the sugar and salt, stirring as you go.
Simmer on low, uncovered, for 6-7 minutes until the gravy coats the back of a spoon.
steps.tip: Keep it below a rolling boil or the coconut milk will separate into grains and oil.

steps.text: Return the prawns with the slit green chillies and cook exactly 2 minutes.
steps.tip: The moment a prawn curls into a tight O it is overdone. A loose C is right.

steps.text: Turn off the heat, stir in the ghee and garam masala, and cover for 5 minutes before serving with plain rice.

storage: Keeps 1 day refrigerated. Reheat gently over low heat only until warm — reheating hard makes the prawns rubbery and splits the coconut milk.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
nutrition.caveat: Ingredients given to taste rather than by weight are counted as zero, so the real figure is a little higher than this. The + says so.
